issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect PersonService::addParent to return a Person (the saved/updated person). The template's PersonService declares addParent as returning Person (and currently returns null), and PersonResource calls person = personService.addParent(...). However, in the solution repository PersonService::addParent is implemented with a void return type. Meanwhile the solution's PersonResource and PersonServiceTest still call/assign a return value from addParent. This creates an internal contradiction in the solution (method signature vs. usages) and a cross-artifact inconsistency between solution and template/problem. It will cause compile-time errors or confusion for students about the correct signature and expected behavior of addParent.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the solution repository's PersonService::addParent signature and implementation match the problem statement and template: change the method to return Person and return the result of personRepository.save(person). For example, declare 'public Person addParent(Person person, Person parent) { ... return personRepository.save(person); }'. Alternatively, if a void method was intended, update PersonResource and the tests to not expect/assign a return value — but the first option (returning the saved Person) aligns with the problem description and the template and is the recommended fix.
